# 4 Ezra Chapter 8 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 8:3 — summary sentence

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Many-are-created but-few-shall-be-saved" | Literal; hyphenated |
| LOGOS | "Many are created, but few shall be saved" | Same, without hyphens |
| PNEUMA | "Many are created. Few will be saved." | Split into two sentences |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Many are created, but few shall be saved" (LOGOS). Keeping as one sentence preserves the adversative force of the Latin conjunction.

---

## 8:4 — Ezra's self-address

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Swallow then your-understanding, O-my-soul, and-let-your-heart devour-wisdom" | Literal, hyphenated |
| LOGOS | "Swallow then your understanding, O my soul, and let your heart devour wisdom" | Natural formal English |
| PNEUMA | "Soul, absorb what you have been told. Heart, take wisdom into yourself and hold it." | Looser paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Swallow then your understanding, O my soul, and let your heart devour wisdom" (LOGOS). The unusual verbs (swallow/devour) should be preserved — they are striking and intentional.

---

## 8:19 — editorial bracket: Ezra's prayer

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "[This is the beginning of-the-words-of-Ezra's prayer...]" | Bracketed editorial notation |
| LOGOS | "[This is the beginning of the words of Ezra's prayer...]" | Same without hyphens |
| PNEUMA | "[Here begins Ezra's prayer, spoken before he was taken up:]" | Rephrased but same content |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "[This is the beginning of the words of Ezra's prayer, before he was taken up. And he said:]" (LOGOS). The formal phrasing is more consistent with the rest of the translation.

---

## 8:41 — the farmer parable

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "not-all-which-were-sown-shall-come-up-in-due-season, and-not-all-that-were-planted-shall-take-root" | Full literal with hyphens |
| LOGOS | "not all that were sown shall come up in due season, and not all that were planted shall take root" | Clean formal |
| PNEUMA | "not all the seeds will sprout on schedule, and not all the seedlings will take root" | More natural paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS. "Come up in due season" is both more literal and more evocative than "sprout on schedule."

---

## 8:51 — the catalogue of eschatological goods

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "paradise-is-opened, the-tree-of-life-is-planted, plenteousness-is-made-ready, a-city-is-builded" | Literal hyphenated list |
| LOGOS | "paradise is opened, the tree of life is planted, plenteousness is made ready, a city is built" | Same without hyphens; "built" instead of "builded" |
| PNEUMA | "paradise has been opened... a city has been built" | Perfect tense throughout |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS simple present passive ("is opened," "is planted," "is built"). More vivid than PNEUMA's perfect tense.

---

## Total disagreements: 5
